target_customer: Software companies, mainly sales and go to market tool vendors, that need native integrations with their customers' CRMs and other GTM tools
problem: Building and maintaining CRM integrations in house is costly because of varied authentication, changing APIs, rate limits, limited webhooks and data transformation.
business_model: Developer API platform with usage and plan based pricing for unified APIs, actions API and managed data pipelines
product_category: Unified API and integration platform for GTM tools

founders.name: Avery Yip
education: UC Berkeley, computer science and data science
founders.background_notes: YC page: helped Productiv grow from Series A with under 10 customers to Series C with over 100.

founders.name: Zachary Kirby
founders.background_notes: YC page also lists Accel Scholar, Glynn Capital Investment Fellow and Cal Hacks Executive Director.

exit.reason: YC lists the company as Inactive, but vessel.dev was live with demo, pricing and docs links and no shutdown notice.

competitors.name: Apideck
competitors.what: Unified API including a CRM API

technical_complexity.rationale: A unified read and write interface over 8 CRM objects with webhooks for platforms that lack them, plus rate limit handling, is standard but laborious API engineering per the YC launch post.

defensibility.rationale: Once integrated, customers face switching costs, but unified API vendors were many and the connector library can be rebuilt by rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A Product Hunt commenter in March 2022 said Apideck's CRM API would be a direct competitor. No source shows an incumbent acquiring or copying Vessel.

market_need_then: The YC launch post frames CRM integration as costly for every SaaS vendor, and a competing launch on the same Product Hunt page shows others saw the same need.

branding.domain_note: Used vessel.dev; launch materials pointed to vessel.land. A Montreal fund management company also called Vessel exists and a 2016 video service named Vessel closed, so the name collides.
branding.community_and_virality: Sacra published an interview describing Vessel as the Vercel for integrations; no merch or community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Developer interest and a Sacra interview exist, but the name is generic and shared with unrelated companies.

pivots.to: Developer first native integration platform across GTM tools
pivots.why: Sacra and Product Hunt coverage describe broadening beyond CRM; reasons not sourced

outcome_analysis: Vessel launched a CRM unified API in March 2022 and then widened to a native integration platform for GTM tools. YC marks it Inactive, but the product site was live under Kinit Inc and no shutdown or acquisition news was found, so the cause of any failure is not public. Later funding found under the name Vessel belongs to a different company.
notes: The $500K YC convertible note on 2022-03-30 rests on a single database. The $7.5M June 2025 seed (Inovia, Afore) belongs to Vessel Funds of Montreal, an investor management platform, and is excluded. A Welcome to the Jungle page mentions a Bain Capital Ventures and Accel seed and a $0.2m seed in March 2022; this is unverified and may refer to another Vessel. Merge, Finch and Paragon were not confirmed as dated rivals.
